I saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Before calculating them, I checked the method against your Q2 reference: it reproduces all 10 Q2 values exactly.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | `smb`, 300,014,989원 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 249 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | `acc`, 254,927,660원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-08 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u198@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 232 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 703,377원 |
| h. September vs. August growth | -6.3% |

To match the Q2 numbers, I had to read the data in three ways your definitions don't spell out:

- **Dates:** order times are stored in UTC, so I converted them to Korean time (UTC+9) before assigning them to a quarter and month. Some orders sit right at the boundary, such as 2025-09-30T15:30Z, which is October 1 in Korean time and so falls outside Q3.
- **Customers:** the 300 customer records contain only 250 distinct emails. For b, e and f, I treated records with the same email as one customer.
- **Segments:** labels come with inconsistent spacing and capitalization (e.g. `' consumer'`, `'SMB'`), so I trimmed and lowercased them. Each order uses the segment on its own customer record, even when another record with the same email has a different segment.

I tested 12 combinations of these choices, and only this one matched every Q2 value.
